explanation.title: Ser vs Estar: Two Ways to Say 'To Be'

sections.subtitle: When to Use SER
sections.content: Use SER for permanent or essential characteristics: identity (Soy María), profession (Es profesor), origin (Somos de España), nationality (Son mexicanos), material (Es de madera), time/dates (Son las tres, Es lunes), events/location of events (La fiesta es aquí), possession (Es mi libro), descriptions of inherent qualities (Ella es inteligente, El libro es interesante).

sections.subtitle: When to Use ESTAR
sections.content: Use ESTAR for temporary states and locations: physical location (Estoy en casa, Madrid está en España), temporary conditions (Estoy cansado, Está enfermo), emotions/moods (Estamos felices), progressive tenses (Estoy comiendo), results of actions (La puerta está abierta), ongoing states (El agua está caliente). Location of people and things always uses ESTAR, but events use SER.

sections.subtitle: Adjectives That Change Meaning
sections.content: Some adjectives mean different things with SER vs ESTAR: ser listo (to be smart) / estar listo (to be ready), ser rico (to be rich) / estar rico (to be delicious), ser aburrido (to be boring) / estar aburrido (to be bored), ser bueno (to be good person) / estar bueno (to be tasty/attractive), ser malo (to be bad/evil) / estar malo (to be sick/spoiled).

sections.subtitle: With Past Participles
sections.content: With past participles (-ado/-ido forms): SER + past participle = passive voice (action performed by someone): 'El libro fue escrito por Cervantes' (The book was written by Cervantes). ESTAR + past participle = result of an action (state): 'La ventana está rota' (The window is broken - current state). The participle agrees in gender/number with the subject.

sections.subtitle: Progressive Forms with ESTAR
sections.content: ESTAR (never SER) is used for progressive tenses to show ongoing actions: Present progressive: estoy hablando (I am talking), Past progressive: estaba comiendo (I was eating), Future progressive: estaré estudiando (I will be studying). Use gerund (-ando/-iendo) with ESTAR to emphasize action in progress.

sections.subtitle: Fixed Expressions & Tips
sections.content: Common fixed expressions: estar de acuerdo (to agree), estar de moda (to be in fashion), ser hora de (to be time to), estar por (to be about to), estar para (to be in the mood for). Memory tip: SER for permanent 'essence' (who/what something IS), ESTAR for temporary 'state' (how/where something IS RIGHT NOW). Think: PTO-LEC (Profession-Time-Origin / Location-Emotion-Condition).

questions.question: Which verb do you use for 'I am a teacher'?
questions.hint: Professions and occupations always use SER.

questions.question: Which verb do you use for 'I am in the house'?
questions.hint: Physical location of people and things always uses ESTAR.

questions.question: 'Soy de México' means...
questions.hint: Origin and nationality use SER. 'De' indicates where you're FROM.

questions.question: 'Estoy cansado' means...
questions.hint: Temporary physical or emotional states use ESTAR. Tiredness is temporary.

questions.question: Which is correct for 'She is intelligent' (personality trait)?
questions.hint: Inherent characteristics and personality traits use SER.

questions.question: Which is correct for 'It is 3 o'clock'?
questions.hint: Time and dates always use SER. Use 'son' (plural) for hours except 1:00.

questions.question: Which is correct for 'Today is Monday'?
questions.hint: Days of the week and dates use SER.

questions.question: 'Es de madera' means...
questions.hint: Material/composition uses SER with 'de'. What something is MADE OF.

questions.question: Which is correct for 'Madrid is in Spain' (location)?
questions.hint: Geographic location uses ESTAR, even for permanent locations like cities.

questions.question: Which is correct for 'The party is here' (event location)?
questions.hint: Events and their locations use SER, not ESTAR. The party as an event 'is' here.

questions.question: 'Es listo' means...
questions.hint: With SER, 'listo' means smart/clever (personality trait).

questions.question: 'Está listo' means...
questions.hint: With ESTAR, 'listo' means ready/prepared (temporary state).

questions.question: 'El helado está rico' means...

answers.text: The ice cream is good quality

questions.hint: With ESTAR, 'rico' means delicious/tasty when referring to food.

questions.question: 'Es rico' means...
questions.hint: With SER, 'rico' means rich/wealthy (economic status).

questions.question: 'Estoy aburrido' means...
questions.hint: With ESTAR, 'aburrido' means bored (feeling).

questions.question: 'Es aburrido' means...
questions.hint: With SER, 'aburrido' means boring (characteristic of the person/thing).

questions.question: Which verb is used for passive voice with past participles?
questions.hint: SER + past participle = passive voice (action by someone). Example: fue escrito (was written).

questions.question: 'La ventana está rota' means...

answers.text: The window was broken by someone

questions.hint: ESTAR + past participle shows the RESULT or current STATE.

questions.question: Which verb is used for progressive tenses?
questions.hint: ESTAR + gerund = progressive. Estoy comiendo (I am eating), never 'soy comiendo'.

questions.question: How do you say 'I am eating' (right now)?
questions.hint: Use ESTAR conjugated + gerund for actions in progress.

questions.question: 'Estar de acuerdo' means...
questions.hint: This is a fixed expression with ESTAR meaning 'to agree'.

questions.question: Memory trick: SER is for ____, ESTAR is for ____
questions.hint: SER = permanent essence (WHO/WHAT you ARE), ESTAR = temporary state (HOW/WHERE you are NOW).
